source.title: MetricAnything: Scaling Metric Depth Pretraining with Noisy Heterogeneous Sources
source.authors: Baorui Ma; Jiahui Yang; Donglin Di; Xuancheng Zhang; Jianxun Cui; Hao Li; Yan Xie; Wei Chen

record.file_problem: None noted; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines a data-scaling trend in metric depth estimation, an image-domain setting distinct from the language-model scaling claims, but does not fit or test a power law.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a training-data-size sweep for Metric Anything-Pretrain on KITTI depth super-resolution. Other downstream-task results and comparisons do not test the scaling relation and are not rows. No parameter-count or compute sweep, or power-law fit, is reported.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its only scaling result is a six-point training-data-fraction sweep (5%–100%) for one vision model, scored on one downstream benchmark (KITTI 8× depth super-resolution AbsRel). It fits no power law and reports no held-out pretraining loss. It does not vary parameters or compute, and it attempts no extrapolation. The sweep shows monotonic improvement but cannot establish the power-law form V5 names. Per-doubling log-slopes computed from the reported values are irregular (about −0.30, −0.10, −0.40, −0.20). The paper invokes 'the same scaling laws' only as motivation. The finding belongs under fits_no_version, not as a test of V5 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim, 'for the first time', a clear data-scaling trend in metric depth and say the field can benefit from scaling laws like those of foundation models. They also state that scaling of model architecture remains unexplored, and they fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies training-data fraction for an image-based metric-depth model and measures KITTI depth super-resolution AbsRel. It does not use language-model held-out cross-entropy or fit a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.

fits_no_version.finding: For Metric Anything-Pretrain, KITTI 8× depth super-resolution AbsRel falls monotonically from 5.22 to 2.34 as training data rises from 5% to 100% of ~20M pairs. The decline is not a clean power law: per-doubling log-slopes vary between about −0.10 and −0.40. The authors say the model lags PromptDA at small data but leads at full scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In metric depth pretraining from heterogeneous noisy sources, downstream depth error decreases monotonically with training-data size.

fits_no_version.finding: Fig. 2a shows the distilled student trained on 2M, 8M, 12M, 16M and 20M pairs, with zero-shot Middlebury δ1 described as 'consistently higher' with more data. The values are figure-only, and no row records them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-shot metric depth accuracy of the distilled student rises with training-data size.

record.problems: The scaling sweep varies only training-data fraction and reports a downstream depth-estimation error on one benchmark/task. The paper does not report uncertainty for these values or fit a power law, and does not vary parameter count or compute.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-sweep rows were omitted. Other ablations and downstream evaluations do not measure the scaling relation addressed here.

untested.parts: There is no language-model pretraining loss and no sweep of parameters, tokens or compute.
No fit on small runs and no prediction of larger runs.
There is no depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count. The skip-connection ablation compares designs, not shape at fixed size.
The vision data sweep is reported, but no power-law form is fitted or claimed quantitatively. Model-size scaling is explicitly 'unexplored' (Limitations).
Downstream performance is measured at only six data fractions. Its relation to scale is not fitted, and its predictability is not assessed.
No exponents and no comparison of fitting methods.

record.verdict_notes: The record listed relation 'tests' with every version 'not_tested', which is inconsistent; it is corrected here to discusses/T6. The data sweep uses downstream AbsRel on a single benchmark, with no uncertainty and one run per fraction. The student data sweep in Fig. 2a (δ1 on Middlebury) is figure-only and has no row. Other experiments (radar fine-tuning, VLM/VLA transfer, test-time resolution, prompt density) are method evaluations, not scaling tests.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss, parameter/token/compute sweep, or power-law fit is reported.
No power laws fitted on smaller runs or predictions evaluated on larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is tested.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count as a test of loss.
The study reports a data-size performance trend in metric depth, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in this modality or other training regimes.
Downstream results are reported, but the study does not test whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents, fit-method comparison, or evidence of setup-dependent power-law curvature or disagreement is reported.
